# ngwr

> Angular UI library — standalone, signals-first, zoneless, fully tree-shakable.
> Over two hundred secondary entry points, built on `@angular/cdk` primitives.
> No runtime dependencies. Docs and live demos: https://ngwr.dev
> Source: https://github.com/thekhegay/ngwr

This file orients AI agents and LLMs that consume ngwr. For exact, current
component APIs, read the bundled TypeScript types
(`node_modules/ngwr/types/ngwr-<name>.d.ts`). ngwr.dev is prerendered, so
fetching a route returns real HTML you can read; the machine-readable resources
listed at the bottom are still the faster path for bulk API lookups.

## Docs map

ngwr.dev has six sections:

- `/docs/*` — getting started: introduction, installation, configuration
  (`provideWr()`), migration, the agent skill and the MCP server.
  e.g. https://ngwr.dev/docs/installation
- `/guides/*` — how to use a subsystem: theming, tokens, forms, overlays,
  translations, SSR, testing. e.g. https://ngwr.dev/guides/forms
- `/reference/<kind>/<name>` — one page per public API; `<kind>` is
  components, directives, pipes, services, utils, validators or interfaces.
  e.g. https://ngwr.dev/reference/components/select
- `/charts/<name>` — the charts. e.g. https://ngwr.dev/charts/bar-chart
- `/icons/<set>` — the icon-set browsers. e.g. https://ngwr.dev/icons/lucide
- `/bits/<name>` — animation and visual-effect components.
  e.g. https://ngwr.dev/bits/aurora

## Install

Preferred — the schematic installs ngwr + its peers, adds `@use 'ngwr/theme'` to
your global styles, and prints a tailored provider snippet to paste into bootstrap:

```
ng add ngwr
```

Or add it manually (pnpm / npm / yarn):

```
pnpm add ngwr @angular/cdk
```

Requires Angular 22.2 or a later 22.x: the `@angular/*` peers are `^22.2.0` (`@angular/cdk`,
`@angular/common`, `@angular/core`, `@angular/forms`,
`@angular/platform-browser`), plus `rxjs ^7`. A newer Angular major joins the
range in a release once CI has run the suite on it. Optional: `@angular/router`,
which `wr-sidebar`, a breadcrumb `routerLink` and the two router adapters need,
and the eight `prosemirror-*` packages that only `ngwr/editor` imports. Icon
sets such as `lucide` are not peers, since `lucideIcons()` and `svgIcon()` take
the icon data. Outside that range npm refuses the install with `ERESOLVE`, while
pnpm and yarn only warn; on Angular 21 or older the `ng build` then fails in the
linker with `Unsupported enum value for [object Object]`. There is no `engines`
field and no TypeScript peer: both come from your Angular. Browsers: Chrome 123,
Firefox 120, Safari 17.5 or newer, since the theme uses `light-dark()`.
Compatibility per major: https://ngwr.dev/docs/installation

**There is no root barrel: `import { X } from 'ngwr'` is wrong for every
component.** The root entry point exports only `provideWr()`, so an IDE
auto-import of a component from it gives `TS2305` and no hint. Every symbol
comes from its entry point — `import { WrButton } from 'ngwr/button'` — and for
most components the entry point is the last segment of the docs URL. Not for
all of them: charts and bits are nested, so `/charts/bar-chart` is
`ngwr/charts/bar-chart` and `/bits/aurora` is `ngwr/bits/aurora`;
`/reference/components/qrcode` is `ngwr/qr`, `form-field` is
`ngwr/form` and `button-group` is `ngwr/button`, while the
directive, pipe, util and validator pages share `ngwr/directives`, `ngwr/pipes`,
`ngwr/utils` and `ngwr/validators`. Each page's import snippet names the right
one. Mind the ones that do not match the selector: `<wr-btn>` and
`<wr-btn-group>` are `ngwr/button`, `<wr-tag>` is `ngwr/badge`, `<wr-option>` is
`ngwr/select`, `<wr-accordion>` is `ngwr/collapse`, `<wr-form-field>` is
`ngwr/form`, `<wr-kbd>` is `ngwr/keyboard`, `<wr-count-up>` is `ngwr/counter`,
and `[wrAutofocus]`, `[wrAutosize]`, `[wrClickOutside]` and
`[wrCopyToClipboard]` are `ngwr/directives`.

Styles: in your global SCSS, `@use 'ngwr/theme'` first, then one
`@use 'ngwr/<name>'` per component a template renders; there is no
`@use 'ngwr'` umbrella. Only a module's first load can be configured, so
`@use 'ngwr/theme' with (…)` below a component line fails the build. A
component's sheet brings the sheets of what it renders inside (`ngwr/table`
styles its checkboxes and pager). **Two kinds of sheet need a line although no
template names them**, and nothing warns without them: `ngwr/density` with
`withDensity()` or `[wrDensity]` (nothing else declares the `--wr-density-*`
multipliers, so density silently does nothing), and the sheet of a component a
service opens — `WrDialog.open()` needs `ngwr/dialog`, `WrToast.show()`
`ngwr/toast`, `WrDrawerManager.open()` `ngwr/drawer`, `WrWindowManager.open()`
`ngwr/window` and `WrTour.start()` `ngwr/tour`. Optional sheets no component
needs: `ngwr/reset`, `ngwr/grid`, `ngwr/typography-utilities`,
`ngwr/breakpoints` (mixins for your own SCSS) and `ngwr/animations` (keyframes
and animation classes; the animation components are `ngwr/bits/*`).
`ngwr/reset`, `ngwr/typography-utilities` and `ngwr/animations` load the theme,
so they go below a configured `@use 'ngwr/theme' with (…)` like any component
line. Details: https://ngwr.dev/docs/installation

## Providers (main.ts)

App-wide configuration is ONE call, `provideWr()` from `ngwr` (the root entry
point's only export), taking a feature per setting, each imported from the entry
point it configures — only the features an app imports are bundled:

```ts
import { provideWr } from 'ngwr';
import { withDensity } from 'ngwr/density';
import { withToast } from 'ngwr/toast';
import { withDates } from 'ngwr/date';

providers: [
  provideWr(
    withDensity({ defaultDensity: 'sm' }),
    withToast({ duration: 6000 }),
    withDates({ locale: 'ru-RU' }),
  ),
],
```

The features are `withDensity` (`ngwr/density`), `withTheme` (`ngwr/theme`),
`withToast` (`ngwr/toast`), `withDates` (`ngwr/date`), `withStorage`
(`ngwr/storage`), `withMeta` (`ngwr/meta`) and `withWindows` (`ngwr/window`).
Every one is optional, the same
feature twice throws in dev mode, and all but `withDates` configure a root
service, so they belong at bootstrap rather than in a route. The theme needs no
feature: the `--wr-*` tokens are plain CSS and dark mode follows
`color-scheme`; `withTheme()` only changes the default and boots `WrTheme`
(Theme, below). There is no `provideWrDensity()`, `provideWrToastConfig()`,
`provideWrStorage()`, `provideWrMeta()`, `provideWrTheme()` or
`provideWrDateAdapter()` since v15. Details:
https://ngwr.dev/docs/configuration

The rest are calls of their own, added from their entry points as needed:

- `provideWrOverlay()` is gone (v15), because overlays need no provider: every
  overlay (dialog / select / dropdown / popover / toast / drawer) renders into
  ngwr's own CDK overlay container, `.wr-overlay-container`, so it never
  collides with Material, NG-ZORRO or other CDK consumers. `WrVisualViewport`
  and `--wr-keyboard-inset` went with it; read `window.visualViewport` for the
  keyboard inset. Overlays always float; a sheet on a phone is a
  `<wr-drawer position="bottom">` you open yourself.
- `provideWrIcons(lucideIcons({ check: Check }))` — icon registry (`ngwr/icon`,
  which holds `lucideIcons()` too; every other set, feather included, registers
  its raw SVG with `svgIcon()`).
- `ngwr/config` and `provideWrConfig()` are gone (v15): `size` and `rounded`
  default to the value written on the input. Bind them where you want another
  value, or wrap the component in your own.
- `provideWrI18n(...)` + `provideWrI18nBaseCatalogs({ en: wrEn })` +
  `provideWrI18nStaticLoader(...)` — localization. ngwr's catalogs go in as a
  BASE, never spread into yours: a spread is shallow, so any namespace you share
  with ngwr, e.g. `common`, `form`, `table`, keeps only the side spread
  last, and the other side's keys stop resolving with nothing logged — ngwr's
  components fall back to English and a `wrT` read renders the raw key.
- Calendar, event calendar and date-picker need no date provider:
  `WrDateAdapter` resolves to the native adapter (`Date` + `Intl`, locale from
  `LOCALE_ID`). `provideWr(withDates({ locale }))` (`ngwr/date`) pins another
  locale; for another date library, extend `WrDateAdapter` and pass the class as
  `withDates({ adapter })`. Its `format` and `parse` handle every `WrDateFormat`
  key, including the `12h`, `24h` and `Seconds` variants of `time` and
  `shortDateTime` (`time24h`, `shortDateTime12hSeconds`) that v15 added.

Injected rather than provided: `WrTour` (`ngwr/tour`) runs a guided onboarding
tour — `tour.start([{ target: '[data-tour="save"]', content: '…' }])` spotlights
one element at a time; a step whose target is missing is skipped, not floated.

## Schematics — let `ng` wire it

- `ng add ngwr` — installs peers, adds `@use 'ngwr/theme'` to styles, prints provider setup.
- `ng g ngwr:use WrFoo --path src/app/x.ts` — adds the import + splices `WrFoo` into that
  component's `@Component` imports.
- `ng g ngwr:provider <name>` — splices a provider into the app's providers:
  `provideWrIcons()`, `provideWrI18n()` or `provideWrLoadingBarRouter()`, or a
  feature inside `provideWr()`: `withToast()`, `withDensity()`, `withStorage()`
  or `withTheme()`. Density also needs `@use 'ngwr/density'` in your styles.
- `ng g ngwr:icon-set` — scaffolds a tree-shaken icon barrel.
- `ng g ngwr:component-style <name>` — adds `@use 'ngwr/<name>'` to the global
  stylesheet, after the theme line and after the last `@use` already there.
  Every component a template renders needs its line. A name from before v15
  (`bar-chart`) lands on its nested entry point (`ngwr/charts/bar-chart`).
- `ng g ngwr:page <form|table|dashboard>` — starter page wired with ngwr.
- `ng update ngwr` — runs upgrade migrations.

## Upgrading

Run `ng update ngwr` once, from whatever major the app is on. It installs the
latest release and runs every migration between the installed version and that
release, in order. Do not step through the majors, and never target a 7.x, 8.x or
9.x release: their schematics die with `exports is not defined in ES module
scope`. A migration rewrites what is a pure rename and REPORTS, by file (by
file and line for v15), what needs a decision only the app can make. Read its output, because the reported
half is where the silent failures are. Every breaking change, newest first, each
with a diff: https://ngwr.dev/docs/migration

Names older majors used, which code written for them (and a model trained on
that code) still spells. Each major's migration rewrites them, v15's included:
`ng update ngwr` runs `migration-v15`, which moves the paths, the provider
calls, the readable `-rgb` reads and the renamed token reads, and lists the
rest. The lists below are the ones an agent most often meets;
https://ngwr.dev/docs/migration is the complete list.

- v15, providers: `provideWrDensity`, `provideWrToastConfig`,
  `provideWrStorage`, `provideWrMeta`, `provideWrTheme` and
  `provideWrDateAdapter` are `withDensity`, `withToast`, `withStorage`,
  `withMeta`, `withTheme` and `withDates`, passed to one `provideWr()` from
  `ngwr` (a bare `provideWrDateAdapter()` just goes: the native adapter is the
  default). A `WR_THEME_CONFIG` provider is `withTheme()` too, which also boots
  `WrTheme`. `WrDateAdapterOptions` and `ProvideWrStorageOptions` are
  `WrDatesOptions` and `WrStorageOptions`. `provideWrOverlay()`,
  `provideWrConfig()`, `provideWrResponsiveOverlays()` and
  `provideWrFormErrors()` are gone, with `WR_CONFIG`, `useConfigValue()`,
  `WR_RESPONSIVE_OVERLAYS`, `wrPresentAsSheet`, `WR_FORM_ERRORS` and
  `WR_FORM_ERROR_FALLBACKS`.
- v15, paths: every chart and animation entry point is nested, so
  `ngwr/bar-chart` is `ngwr/charts/bar-chart` and `ngwr/aurora` is
  `ngwr/bits/aurora`; `ngwr/drag-drop` is `ngwr/sortable-list`, and the list no
  longer owns its loop — write your own, one `<wr-sortable-item>` per row, with
  no `trackBy`; `ngwr/icon/adapters/lucide` is `ngwr/icon` (`lucideIcons`,
  `lucide` and `LucideIconNode` keep their names). Gone outright:
  `ngwr/icon/adapters/feather` (register feather's own SVG files with
  `svgIcon()`); `ngwr/date/adapters/fns` and `ngwr/date/adapters/luxon` (use the
  native adapter or your own `WrDateAdapter` subclass, and note that a date-fns
  token `[format]` such as `EEEE` or `PPP` prints verbatim on the native one);
  `ngwr/config`; `ngwr/media` (use the CDK's `BreakpointObserver`);
  `ngwr/markdown` (use `<wr-editor readonly [toolbar]="false">`);
  `ngwr/squircle` (`wrSquircle` is `shape="squircle"` on `wr-btn`, `wr-avatar`
  and `wr-badge`, or the `theme.smooth-br()` mixin elsewhere); and
  `ngwr/action-sheet` (a `<wr-drawer position="bottom" rounded>` with your own
  rows). `@use 'ngwr'` and `@use 'ngwr/overlay'` no longer resolve.
- v15, tokens: `--wr-color-light` and `--wr-color-outline` are
  `--wr-border-base`; `--wr-color-border`, `--wr-color-border-subtle` and
  `--wr-color-border-strong` are all `--wr-border-subtle`, or
  `--wr-border-base` for a firmer line. `--wr-border-strong` is new, and darker
  than any v14 border, so it replaces none of them. `--wr-color-dark`, and the
  dark theme's `--wr-color-white-contrast`, are `--wr-color-on-surface`, and
  `--wr-color-medium` and `--wr-color-muted-text` are
  `--wr-color-on-surface-muted`. Every `-rgb` token is gone:
  `--wr-color-backdrop-rgb` is the colour `--wr-color-backdrop`,
  `--wr-calendar-accent-rgb` is `--wr-calendar-accent`, `--wr-color-picker-rgb`
  is `--wr-color-picker-color`, and the rest become a `color-mix()`.
  `wrThemeTokens()`, `wrIntentTokens()` and `wrContrastFor()` are gone (rebrand
  at build time with `$base-colors` or `theme.rebrand()`), so are
  `theme.dark-selector()` and `$theme-attribute`, and code that read
  `data-theme` reads `WrTheme.resolved()`.
- v15, components: `[wrTypography]`'s `tone="dark"` and `tone="medium"` are
  `tone="base"` and `tone="muted"`; `<wr-timeline-item color="medium">` is
  `color="neutral"`; a `WrSidebarItem`'s `badge: 'new'` and `badge: '12'` are
  `badge: { text: 'New', tone: 'primary' }` and `count: 12`, and a
  `WrSidebarGroup` child can itself be a group, so check `'children' in child`
  before reading `url`.
- v14: `<wr-alert closeable>` is `closable`; `[wrInput]`'s `wrSize` is `size`;
  `<wr-table [totalItems]>` is `[total]`; `<wr-pagination [(currentPage)]>` and
  `(currentPageChange)` are `[(page)]` and `(pageChange)`;
  `isDisabledWhenLoading` is `disabledWhenLoading`; the window `chromeSize`
  values `'compact' | 'normal'` are `'sm' | 'md'`.
- v12: `ngwr/date-adapter` is `ngwr/date`; `ngwr/date-adapter-fns` and
  `ngwr/date-adapter-luxon` moved under `ngwr/date/adapters/`, which v15
  removed.
- v9: a grouped `<wr-checkbox value="…">` is `checkboxValue`.
- v8: the density values `compact` / `default` / `comfortable` are `sm` / `md`
  / `lg`.
- v7: classes lost their suffix (`WrButtonComponent` is `WrButton`,
  `WrToastService` is `WrToast`), `[wrTooltip]` is `[wrPopover]` with
  `mode="tooltip"`, `ngwr/tag` is `ngwr/badge` and `ngwr/form-field` is
  `ngwr/form`.

Changes no migration rewrites. All but the last fail silently:

- Dark mode is `color-scheme` plus `light-dark()` (v15): `[data-theme]` and
  every `-rgb` token are gone, so a `[data-theme='dark']` selector matches
  nothing and a `var(--wr-…-rgb)` the codemod could not read drops the whole
  declaration holding it (see Theme, below). The same major removed the `secondary`, `light`,
  `medium` and `dark` intents; which intent each use becomes is the app's call.
  Without `strictTemplates` a removed `color` value renders neutral, and a
  `var()` at any removed token drops its whole declaration.
- Inputs v15 removed still compile as plain attributes and do nothing: a bare
  `wrSquircle`, `<wr-drawer showHandle>`, `responsive` on `wr-select`,
  `[wrDropdown]`, `[wrPopover]` and `wr-command-palette`, and
  `<wr-editor format>`. Rules on `.wr-overlay-sheet`, `.wr-overlay-backdrop`
  and `.wr-command-palette--sheet` match nothing.
- A `<wr-sortable-list>` that still holds an `<ng-template>` renders nothing,
  and `<wr-editor>` refuses an HTML or markdown string, and `''`: its value is
  a `WrEditorJson` tree, or `null` when empty (v15).
- `<wr-sidebar>` draws no icons by default (v15): bind `defaultGroupIcon` and
  `defaultItemIcon` to keep them. Its row classes were renamed in the same
  release — `.wr-sidebar__entry` and `.wr-sidebar__item` are `.wr-sidebar__row`,
  `.wr-sidebar__group-toggle` is `.wr-sidebar__row--group` and
  `.wr-sidebar__item-title` is `.wr-sidebar__title` — so a rule on the old
  names matches nothing. `--wr-sidebar-padding`, the only sidebar hook v14
  published, is unchanged.
- ngwr ships no validation text (v15). Without a validator's `{ message }` or a
  `validation.<key>` in your own catalog a field shows no error, and only dev
  mode warns.
- `wrDate` with no provider changed its output (v15): `shortDate` from
  `3/15/26` to `3/15/2026`, `time` from `2:30 PM` to `02:30 PM`, and a token
  format such as `'dd.MM.yyyy'` is honoured where it fell back to `shortDate`.
- Deleting `provideWrConfig()` (v15) resets every control it configured to
  `md` and the standard radius: bind those inputs first.
- `<wr-pagination ofLabel>` is gone (v14), and the `pagination.of` catalog key
  with it. The range is one `pagination.range` template with `{{from}}` /
  `{{to}}` / `{{total}}` placeholders, and a catalog still carrying the old key
  reverts that line to English.
- `[id]` on `<wr-checkbox>`, `<wr-radio>` and `<wr-switch>` goes to the inner
  `<input>` rather than the host (v13), so a `wr-checkbox#agree` selector stops
  matching. `#agree` alone still works.
- `lucideIcons()` registers its keys verbatim (v9): `{ chevronDown: ChevronDown }`
  is no longer found as `chevron-down`, so quote multi-word keys.
- `readI18nText()` returns a `Signal<string>` (v12). This one is loud: the
  compiler names every call site that needs a `()`.

The router adapters, the `LOCALE_ID` default and the stricter date parsing, all
from v14, are current behaviour and described under Patterns below.

## Use ngwr — don't hand-roll

The catalog is large: prefer an ngwr component, util, pipe, or validator over raw
markup, custom logic, or another library. e.g. use `wr-file-upload`, not a bare
`<input type="file">`; reach for `ngwr/utils`, `ngwr/pipes`, `ngwr/validators`
before writing your own. Full catalog: https://ngwr.dev/reference/components.

## Common components (selector — import)

- **Form** — `wr-btn` (ngwr/button), `wr-speed-dial`, `wrInput` (ngwr/input),
  `wr-textarea`, `wr-select` (ngwr/select; modes single/multi/search/tag, plus
  `searchable` for a multi-with-typeahead and `(searchChange)` for server-side
  search), `wr-checkbox` (form state is `[(checked)]`; inside
  `<wr-checkbox-group>` the identity input is `checkboxValue`, NOT `value`),
  `wr-radio-group` (ngwr/radio), `wr-switch`, `wr-slider`, `wr-segmented`,
  `wr-rating`, `wr-knob`, `wr-input-number`, `wr-input-otp`, `wr-date-picker`
  (date/time/datetime) and `wr-date-range-picker` (both in ngwr/date-picker; the
  range value is `[start, end]`, hence a separate component), `wr-cascader` (the
  value is the whole path), `[wrMention]` (ngwr/mention, on a textarea or input),
  `wr-file-upload`, `wr-form-field` (in ngwr/form), `wr-color-picker`,
  `wr-transfer` (dual listbox; the value is the RIGHT pane), `wr-editor`
  (ngwr/editor — rich text on ProseMirror, an optional peer; the value is the
  document as a JSON tree, `null` when empty, validated against the schema; a
  value it cannot read is refused and the editor keeps its document; an app that
  stores HTML or markdown converts at its own boundary), `wr-schema-form`
  (ngwr/schema-form; draws a form from the `WR_FIELD` metadata on a Signal Forms
  schema, and skips a field that carries none).
- **Data** — `wr-table` (column pin/resize/drag-reorder, row selection,
  expandable rows, grouping, tree rows (`childrenKey`), summary rows,
  CSV export, virtualized body),
  `wr-pagination`, `wr-tree`, `wr-list`, `wr-timeline`, `wr-calendar`,
  `wr-event-calendar` (see Scheduling below), `wr-graph` (read-only layered
  diagram: `nodes` plus `{ from, to }` parent-to-child `edges`, each node a
  default card or an `ng-template wrGraphNode`), `wr-virtual-scroll`,
  `wr-sortable-list` (drag-to-reorder, one `<wr-sortable-item>` per row from
  your own loop, with `[wrDragHandle]` — all in ngwr/sortable-list).
- **Charts** — `wr-line-chart` (`showArea` makes it an area chart and
  `stacked` stacks the series, both for a stacked area), `wr-bar-chart`
  (grouped or `stacked` `series`, `orientation` `'horizontal'`, and `lines`
  drawn over the bars for a combo chart),
  `wr-donut-chart` (`pie` fills it to the centre), `wr-scatter-chart` (numeric
  x and y, a `size` per point for bubbles), `wr-radar-chart` (`variant`
  `'polar-area'` draws wedges), `wr-heatmap-chart`, `wr-funnel-chart`,
  `wr-waterfall-chart`, `wr-treemap-chart`, `wr-bullet-chart`,
  `wr-boxplot-chart`, `wr-candlestick-chart`, `wr-sparkline`, `wr-gauge`,
  `wr-calendar-heatmap`, `wr-meter-group`, each its
  own entry point at `ngwr/charts/<name>` (`ngwr/charts/bar-chart`), documented
  under https://ngwr.dev/charts/, themed through the `--wr-*` tokens and each
  with a hover tooltip. `ul[wr-chart-legend]` (ngwr/charts/chart-legend) is the
  legend the bar, line, donut, meter-group, scatter and radar charts draw, and
  a key of its own beside several charts; `toggleableLegend` on those charts
  makes each row a `<button aria-pressed>` over a `hiddenSeries`
  (`hiddenSegments` on donut and meter group, and `hiddenLines` for the bar
  chart's lines) model. Bar, line, scatter, radar, heatmap-chart,
  calendar-heatmap, funnel, waterfall, treemap, box plot and candlestick take
  an opt-in `dataTable` that renders their figures as a visually hidden table
  for screen readers. Every chart writes its numbers with `Intl.NumberFormat`
  in `LOCALE_ID` (line-chart ticks and bar-chart labels compact from a thousand
  up, `5K`, unless the full numbers are shorter; tooltips never), and takes
  `valueFormat: (value: number) => string` for any other format (the waterfall
  passes a second argument saying where the figure goes, so a formatter can go
  compact on the drawing alone).
- **Feedback** — `wr-alert`, `wr-result`, `wr-empty`, `wr-skeleton`,
  `wr-spinner`, `wr-progress`, `wr-loading-bar`.
- **Layout / Display** — `wr-layout` (with header / sider / content / footer),
  `wr-page-header`, `wr-card`, `wr-divider`, `wr-carousel`, `wr-collapse`,
  `wr-splitter`, `wr-toolbar`, `wr-descriptions`, `wr-statistic`,
  `wr-avatar`, `wr-badge` and `wr-tag` (both ngwr/badge), `wr-qr` (ngwr/qr),
  `wr-lightbox`, `wr-image-cropper`, `wr-compare`, `wr-pull-to-refresh`. There
  is no markdown renderer since v15: a stored rich-text document is shown by
  `<wr-editor readonly>`, which mounts no ProseMirror.
- **Navigation** — `wr-tabs`, `wr-stepper`, `wr-breadcrumbs`, `wr-anchor`,
  `wr-sidebar` (follows the active route by injecting `Router`),
  `wr-back-top`, `[wrAffix]`, `wr-dropdown-menu` (with its `[wrDropdown]`
  trigger — both in ngwr/dropdown).
- **Overlays** — `wr-drawer` (or `WrDrawerManager.open()` to open a component as
  a drawer from code; with `hasBackdrop` off it is a non-modal side panel, with
  no focus trap and no `aria-modal`), `[wrPopover]` (directive; has a
  `tooltip` mode), `wr-command-palette`, `wr-context-menu`, `wr-popconfirm`.
  (Dialog and toast are service-opened — inject `WrDialog` / `WrToast`.
  Content inside a service-opened dialog or drawer can `inject(WrDialogRef)` /
  `inject(WrDrawerRef)` to close itself. Windows are service-opened too: there
  is no `<wr-window>`, `WrWindowManager.open()` (ngwr/window) opens one and
  moves focus into it (`autoFocus: false` for a background window), and
  `<wr-window-taskbar>` lists the minimized ones, or every window with
  `show="all"`. Alt+F7 / Alt+F8 move and resize the focused window from the
  keyboard, and the manager can `cascade()`, `tile()` and cycle the active
  window.)
- **Bits** — the animation and visual-effect components: text effects, cursor
  effects, backgrounds and blocks, each its own entry point at
  `ngwr/bits/<name>` (`ngwr/bits/aurora`), documented under
  https://ngwr.dev/bits/ and listed in `llms-full.txt`. Not to be confused with
  `@use 'ngwr/animations'`, the keyframe sheet.

## Patterns

- **Forms** — the value controls are signal-forms native (`FormValueControl`,
  or `FormCheckboxControl` for checkbox/switch), and there is no
  `ControlValueAccessor` in the library. One public class with a `value` model
  implements neither: `[wrColorPickerTrigger]`, a trigger that drives a
  `<wr-color-picker>`, which does.
  Bind `[formField]="form.x"`, use the two-way model standalone (`[(value)]`, or
  `[(checked)]` on checkbox/switch), or classic `[(ngModel)]` / reactive forms
  via Angular's bridge. **That bridge is not an accessor and does not behave like
  one**, and the differences are silent: template validator attributes
  (`required`, `minlength`, `pattern`, …) on an ngwr control are never applied,
  so validators belong on the `FormControl`; `updateOn: 'blur'` / `'submit'` do
  not apply to an ngwr control while a native `<input>` in the same group still
  honours them; a `{ emitEvent: false }` write moves the model and leaves the
  control showing the old value; `<wr-select>` compares object values by `===`
  with no `compareWith`. What the bridge carries, what it drops, and what a form
  does about each: https://ngwr.dev/guides/forms
  ngwr ships no validation copy. For an error no `<wr-form-error key>` claims,
  `<wr-form-field>` shows the validator's own `{ message }`, else
  `validation.<key>` from YOUR i18n catalog; with neither it shows nothing, and
  only dev mode warns.
- **Icons** — register via `provideWrIcons`, render `<wr-icon name="check" />`.
- **Router** — only what is about routes touches `@angular/router`:
  `wr-sidebar` injects `Router` to follow the active route, and
  `wr-breadcrumbs-item` renders a `RouterLink` when you pass `routerLink`. The tab
  strip and the loading bar take routing through opt-in adapters instead. A
  `<wr-tab routerLink>` needs `wrTabsRouting` on the strip plus `WrTabsRouting`
  (`ngwr/tabs/router`) in `imports`, and it throws if you forget.
  `<wr-loading-bar>` follows navigation only with
  `provideWrLoadingBarRouter()` (`ngwr/loading-bar/router`), and it does NOT
  throw — without the provider the bar simply never moves.
- **i18n** — `{{ 'key' | wrT }}` (pipe from `ngwr/i18n`). The locale defaults to
  Angular's `LOCALE_ID`, not the browser, for both copy and dates; an app that
  wants the browser's tag writes
  `provideWr(withDates({ locale: navigator.language }))`. A named date format
  (`shortDate`, `time`, …) parses through the same `Intl` formatter that printed
  it, so input it cannot read returns null and leaves the committed value alone.
  A field that must accept a specific pattern takes an explicit token `[format]`.
- **Theme** — CSS custom properties `--wr-color-*`, `--wr-border-radius-*`, …
  from `@use 'ngwr/theme'`, no provider needed. Dark mode is `color-scheme` plus
  `light-dark()`: `:root` declares `color-scheme: light dark`, so the page
  follows the OS with no JavaScript, and `WrTheme.set('light' | 'dark' | 'auto')`
  forces or releases it by writing `color-scheme` on `<html>`. `WrTheme` applies
  a stored choice or a non-`auto` `defaultMode` when it is first injected;
  `provideWr(withTheme({ defaultMode, storageKey }))` configures it and creates
  it at boot, and `wrThemePrePaintScript()` with the same options covers the
  first paint of a prerendered page. There is no
  `[data-theme]`, no `theme.dark` mixin and no `-rgb` token: write your own dark
  values as `color: light-dark(#0f172a, #e6ebf3)`, and a translucent tint as
  `color-mix(in srgb, var(--wr-color-primary) 12%, transparent)`, never
  `rgba(var(--wr-color-primary-rgb), 0.12)`. A canvas cannot draw a
  `light-dark()` value, and `getPropertyValue()` returns it unresolved, so read
  a colour for canvas from an element's computed `color` —
  `resolveCssColor()` (`ngwr/utils`) does exactly that — and redraw a still
  frame from `watchColorScheme(scheme => …)` (`ngwr/utils`, in an injection
  context or with `{ injector }`), which calls back with `'light'` or `'dark'`
  when the page's scheme changes. Two contrast tokens
  per intent, easy to confuse:
  `--wr-color-<intent>-contrast` is the label ON a filled intent;
  `--wr-color-<intent>-ink` is the intent used AS text on a surface or its own
  `-soft` tint. A bare `--wr-color-<intent>` as text clears AA on a plain light
  surface for every intent but `warning`, but still fails on the `-soft`
  tint — which is exactly where outlined / ghost / tinted variants paint it, so use
  `-ink` there. For muted prose use `--wr-color-on-surface-muted`, and for
  placeholder text `--wr-color-placeholder` (never
  `--wr-color-text-faint`, which is decorative only). An intent colour on a tag,
  badge or typography tone is decoration or category: the words carry the state.
- **SSR** — everything renders on the server; the library contains no
  `ngSkipHydration`, so `provideClientHydration()` and `withEventReplay()` need
  nothing from it. Two calls are NOT no-ops there and ship an overlay into a
  cached page: `WrToast.show()` and `WrDialog.open()` (`WrTour.start()` is the
  one that returns early) — guard them with `afterNextRender` or `WrPlatform`'s
  `isBrowser`. A breakpoint signal has no viewport to measure (ngwr ships none
  since v15 removed `ngwr/media`; the CDK's `BreakpointObserver` answers `false`
  until hydration): reflow with the `responsive` container-query modifiers
  rather than a template branch. The scheme needs
  nothing on the server when it follows the OS, since that is CSS; a visitor
  who CHOSE light or dark has that choice in `localStorage`, which a server
  cannot read, so `wrThemePrePaintScript()` (`ngwr/theme`) is the blocking
  `<head>` reader that applies it before first paint, and
  `wrDensityPrePaintScript()` (`ngwr/density`) does the same for a stored
  density: https://ngwr.dev/guides/ssr
- **Mobile** — a `responsive` input reflows layout components (`wr-table`,
  `wr-toolbar`, `wr-stepper`, …; no overlay has one since v15), a `touch`
  density preset enlarges controls, and `WrHaptics` (ngwr/platform) fires
  vibration feedback.
- **Large datasets** — `virtualScroll` is an opt-in input on `wr-table`,
  `wr-tree` and `wr-select` (search mode), alongside the standalone
  `wr-virtual-scroll` wrapper.
- **Testing** — CDK component harnesses ship beside the components they drive, at
  `ngwr/<entry>/testing` (`ngwr/select/testing`, `ngwr/charts/bar-chart/testing`).
  Every control, every overlay and every chart has one: the form controls
  (`button`, `input`, `textarea`, `checkbox`, `switch`, `radio`, `select`,
  `input-number`, `input-otp`, `slider`, `rating`, `file-upload`, `color-picker`,
  `knob`, `segmented`, `editor`, and `form` for `<wr-form-field>`), the overlays
  (`date-picker`, `dropdown`, `popover`, `dialog`, `drawer`,
  `toast`, `context-menu`, `popconfirm`, `command-palette`, `cascader`,
  `mention`), the data views (`table`, `tree`, `graph`), the navigation and
  disclosure set (`tabs`, `stepper`, `carousel`, `pagination`, `collapse`,
  `transfer`), `splitter`, `speed-dial`, `lightbox`, `tour`,
  `calendar`, `event-calendar`, `window`, `image-cropper`, and every bit but
  three. `WrCalendarDayHarness` ships under two entry points, since a date
  picker's popup IS a calendar. `aurora`, `click-spark`, `confetti` and
  `virtual-scroll` deliberately have none: what they do is a canvas or a measured
  viewport, so every honest method would read the same for a working component
  and a broken one.
  Load them with `TestbedHarnessEnvironment` and narrow with
  `WrButtonHarness.with({ text: 'Save' })` instead of querying ngwr's markup.
  Dialog, toast and a service-opened drawer render outside the fixture — load
  those from `documentRootLoader()`; everything else is an element in your
  template, and where its panel is in the overlay the harness reaches it for you,
  scoped to that instance by the id the trigger publishes.
  Many are families: `WrTableHarness` + row / cell / header-cell, `WrTreeHarness`
  + node, `WrCascaderHarness` + column / option, `WrCommandPaletteHarness` +
  group / item, `WrRadioGroupHarness` + radio, `WrSliderHarness` + thumb,
  `WrInputOtpHarness` + box, `WrRatingHarness` + item, `WrContextMenuHarness` +
  item (submenus included), `WrMentionHarness` + option, `WrTransferHarness` +
  pane / item.
  A unit test has no layout, so anything a mouse would drag (slider, rating,
  file-upload's drop zone) is driven by the KEYBOARD or by real events, never by
  coordinates. Guide: https://ngwr.dev/guides/testing
- **Scheduling** — `wr-event-calendar` covers month / week / day in one
  component. `events` is an input the calendar never writes to: a drag emits
  `eventChange` with the proposed start / end, and you apply it. Event `end` is
  EXCLUSIVE. `editable` turns on drag and resize; `Alt` + arrows do the same
  from the keyboard.

## Deciding whether to use it

- **What it is and how it is tested** — the features, the spec counts and the
  three CI tiers: https://ngwr.dev/docs/introduction
- **A live app to try before installing anything** — the StackBlitz starter,
  on ngwr from npm:
  https://stackblitz.com/github/thekhegay/ngwr/tree/main/projects/starter
- **What each major needs and what it broke** — the compatibility table at
  https://ngwr.dev/docs/installation, every breaking change at
  https://ngwr.dev/docs/migration, and the security support window in the
  repository's `SECURITY.md`: the latest major gets every fix, the one before
  it mechanical fixes only.

The shape of the project: one maintainer, MIT, no commercial support. Every
major ships a codemod for each break a codemod can repair, and a reported
diagnosis for the rest; `ng update ngwr` runs them all in order, v15's
included.

Public API is three surfaces and all three move only in a major: the exported
TypeScript, the `.wr-*` BEM class names (every component ships
`ViewEncapsulation.None`), and the `--wr-*` custom properties. `@internal` in a
TSDoc means not API and survives into the published types, so
`grep -rn "@internal" node_modules/ngwr/types` answers it. A few helpers are
exported, unmarked and undocumented — `wrAppendOverlayClose`, `wrMirrorOffsets`,
`wrFollowDirection`, `WrOutsideClick`, `useFormFieldAria`, `isSafeCssValue`, and
a handful of `WR_*` context tokens such as `WR_STEPPER` —
and carry no stability statement; do not build on them.

## Resources (machine-readable)

- This quick-ref: https://ngwr.dev/llms.txt
- Full reference (every entry point + selector + description):
  https://ngwr.dev/llms-full.txt
- **One page as markdown — append `.md` to any docs URL.**
  `https://ngwr.dev/reference/components/select` also serves
  `https://ngwr.dev/reference/components/select.md`: the same page as markdown,
  prose and code samples and API tables, without the site chrome. Prefer it over
  `llms-full.txt` when you already know which component you need. Each HTML page
  advertises its twin as `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`.
- **MCP server — the same files, askable.** `npx -y -p ngwr ngwr-mcp` (a bin
  in the installed package; zero dependencies, JSON-RPC over stdio) exposes
  four tools: `search_ngwr` turns a need into an entry point name,
  `get_ngwr_component` summarises one entry point, `get_ngwr_api` returns a
  class's inputs / models / outputs read out of the shipped `.d.ts`, and
  `get_ngwr_setup` returns the install / `ng g ngwr:use` / provider commands as
  text — it never runs them, and it never reaches outside its own package: no
  network, no commands. It reads the resources listed here rather than
  embedding a copy of them. Client config for Claude Code / Claude Desktop /
  Cursor, and a worked example of each tool:
  https://ngwr.dev/docs/mcp-server
- **Agent skill — the rules, not the catalog.** `skills/ngwr/SKILL.md` in the
  installed package (also at https://ngwr.dev/skills/ngwr/SKILL.md) is about a
  page of the things this library does that a reasonable guess gets wrong: the
  button's selector is `wr-btn`, a checkbox's group identity is `checkboxValue`,
  there is no `ControlValueAccessor`, imports come from the entry point rather
  than a barrel, app-wide config is one `provideWr()`, and there are five
  intents and no `[data-theme]`. `references/catalog.md` and
  `references/setup.md` sit beside it for the long tail. Generated from the same pass as `llms-full.txt`:
  https://ngwr.dev/docs/skills
- All site URLs (for crawlers): https://ngwr.dev/sitemap.xml
- Source, README, per-component `.d.ts` types: https://github.com/thekhegay/ngwr
  (installed at `node_modules/ngwr/types/ngwr-<name>.d.ts`; the package also
  ships `README.md`, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and `skills/ngwr/` — and no
  other markdown: there is no `CHANGELOG.md` in the tarball, and the docs'
  markdown twins are served from ngwr.dev rather than copied into it)
